title: No source names the register's request and answer field names, its marker vocabulary or its read path, and the module FSD and TSD give the tables and the endpoint inventory only
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-020.md, story line RWB-P4-E1064-APP (wt APP, C = [RWB-P1-E1064-CON], H = [], I = [], X = [], patterns DP01, DP05, DP07, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19, acs = []); _work/msr/context/P4.md (tables 5: delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict; REST provided 4: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants; events 0; jobs 1 JOB-18; workflows 0; REST base /api/recovery/access/v1, schema rwb_access, topic rwb.access.events.v1, queue rwb-access); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md (sections 1, 3, 4, 7, 10, 11 and 12: sys_objects, sys_fields, sys_field_version, data_product, data_contract; five admin operations; MSG-P4-002); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.3, A2.4 and A2.5 (field catalogues of role, permission and masking_rule; AC-P4-004-01; AC-EXC-P4-004-02, -03, -05); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T3.1 (role, permission, masking_rule), T3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE, LOV-VERSION-STATUS), T6.1 (RBAC matrix) and appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-021)
section: RWB-P4-E1064-APP sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 13, 15 and 16: the register's path and query parameters, its request and answer field names, the marker vocabulary (masked or clear), the shape of its role part, the coded check names of MSG-P1-002 and the rendering the screen shows
description: The legacy story gives the dictionary's five admin operations and its field set; the TSD P4 appendix gives the module's endpoint inventory, in which the two nearest operations are API-P4-004 GET /admin/lists/{listCode} (Reference data R) and API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles (Platform administration R), and neither reads a dictionary field, its owner role or a masking marker. No source states a register read for the dictionary's field IDs, its query parameters, its answer field names, the vocabulary of its marker, the shape of its role part, or the coded names the refusal of a governance load names. The legacy story also names two identifiers this slice reuses (MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P1-002 for a refused dictionary load) and one it does not (MSG-P7-002 for a maker-approves-own-load refusal, which the module uses in AC-EXC-P4-004-03). The story therefore fixes one read, its parameters and its answer shape in section 12.1, names the marker masked or clear, and carries the placeholder 'Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-020-1; ASM-B2-P4-020-1)' for every field-level detail it cannot copy, inventing no business value.
evidence: wp/B2-P4-020.md APP line (acs empty, so no legacy criterion is copied; wt APP; C holds one entry); context/P4.md provided operations (4, none a dictionary read) and tables (5, none a dictionary table); legacy RWB-E1-064 section 12 (five admin operations on /admin/data-dictionary and /admin/data-contracts only) and section 15 (no screen in the legacy story); FSD P4 v3 A2.3.3.2 and A2.4.3.2 (the field catalogues of role and permission carry role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group, role_id, capability_area and letters only); TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 (the whole endpoint inventory: no dictionary path in it); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (masking_rule fields DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204, with no marker or reason vocabulary); TSD P4 v3 T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS is the only state list of a version)
proposed: Publish the register's path, its query parameters and its answer schema with RWB-P1-E1064-CON so that the dictionary screen and the gate build against one document, and fix the marker vocabulary (masked, clear) and the coded check names of MSG-P1-002 in the Error and Message Standard. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from every placeholder of RWB-P4-E1064-APP and from ASM-B2-P4-020-1.

title: TSD P4 T6.1 gives no role the Reference data A letter that API-P4-006 requires of an approver, so the four-eyes approver of a governance load is unnamed
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T6.1 (RW-DATASTEW R and RU, RW-REFADM R and CRUD, RW-COE CRUD and CRUD, RW-COMPLY R and RU, RW-LEGAL R and RU, RW-SECADM R, R and CRUDA, RW-PLATADM R, R and CRUD; no role holds A in Reference data) and appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2, API-P4-006 (approve a reference data load: Authorization Reference data, right A) and API-P4-005 (submit: right C); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.4.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-004-03 (the loader cannot approve, and only the table's approver role may) and A2.4.3.1 VR-P4-004-1 (MSG-P4-002); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md section 10 (RW-DATASTEW Reference data U, RW-REFADM Reference data C) and section 3 (the ACE team lead confirms, not approves)
section: RWB-P4-E1064-APP sections 3, 4, 7 (AC4, AC9), 10, 12.1, 12.8, 13 and 16 (TC-E1-064-06, TC-E1-064-09): the approver role code, the SIT matrix fixture row that carries A, and the role that may never approve its own load
description: The approve operation of the module declares the Reference data A right (API-P4-006) and the FSD refuses an approval by the loader with MSG-P7-002, but the RBAC matrix of T6.1 gives no role an A letter in Reference data: the letters granted are R, RU, CRUD and, in other areas, CRUDA. The legacy story names the data steward (U) and the reference data administrator (C) and names neither an approver role nor a second-person rule for the dictionary load. So the identity that must perform the four-eyes approval of a governance load cannot be taken from any source, and a story that named one would invent a permission value. This story keeps the letter (A) and the rule (author is not approver) as the sources state them, leaves the role code to the SIT matrix fixture, and records the missing grant here.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 rows read in full: no A in the Reference data column for any of the 41 roles and service identities; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-006 Authorization cell 'Reference data, right A, scope applied'; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-03 (a load's author is refused, the approver role must be a different one) and VR-P4-004-1 (MSG-P4-002); legacy RWB-E1-064 section 10 (RW-DATASTEW and RW-REFADM only); context/P4.md (no permission row and no role of the approver named)
proposed: Add the A letter in Reference data to one role in the next matrix version (a data change under FEAT-ACA-04 and FEAT-ACA-05, no build), name that role as the approver of a reference and dictionary load, and confirm that the same role may not both submit and approve. Until then the SIT fixture carries the A row and the gate refuses every approval where the matrix gives the caller no A, which is the safe direction. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from ASM-B2-P4-020-2.

title: No source states how many of the 1,366 dictionary fields are personal, so the masking coverage the gate checks has no expected count
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md sections 2, 7 (AC1, AC3), 8 (BR1) and 11 (DF-REF-105 sys_fields.is_personal, marked Read); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T3.1 (masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 keyed on role_code, field_id and masking_version) and T3.2 (no personal-field list); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.5 (mask PDPA fields by role) and AC-EXC-P4-004-05 (a personal field with no masking rule is masked); _work/msr/context/P4.md (tables owned by P4)
section: RWB-P4-E1064-APP sections 2, 7 (AC3), 8 (BR4), 11, 12.1, 12.8, 13 and 16 (TC-E1-064-02): the count of personal field IDs the register must cover, the count of masking rows a load must carry, and the completeness measure of the coverage check
description: The dictionary carries an is_personal flag on every field (DF-REF-105) and the masking policy is keyed on field IDs, but no source states how many of the 1,366 fields are personal, how many masking rows the masking version in force should hold, or whether a personal field with no row at all is a defect of the policy or an accepted default. The legacy story's measure is completeness of source, owner, refresh cycle and late behavior only, and it never counts the personal fields. This story therefore asserts the rule and not a number: every personal field ID has at least one row at the masking version in force, a field with no row is masked for every role and is reported as a coverage failure, and the register reports the count it finds instead of a fixed value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-064 section 11 (is_personal is read, with no count) and section 7 AC1 (the completeness list of attributes does not include the personal flag or a masking row); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (masking_rule carries no count, no pack label and no completeness rule); TSD P4 v3 T3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY and the version states only); FSD P4 v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05 (the default is masked, no count); no source lists the personal fields of the 30 views or of the 92 tables
proposed: Publish the personal-field list of the 14 data products from the dictionary (is_personal true) and the masking pack coverage it must reach, so that the gate can fail a load that leaves a personal field uncovered and the SIT run can assert a count. Until then the gate asserts the rule per field ID and reports the count it finds. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from ASM-B2-P4-020-3.

title: No target source states which service applies an approved dictionary load, and the legacy reference-load endpoint no longer exists
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md sections 4 (steps 2 and 3: POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads with table sys_fields, then DataDictionaryLoader.apply) and 12 (the loader is an interface of P1 and the load is approved through /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-005 submit and API-P4-006 approve a reference load) and T5.2 (calls to P3 and P7 through published interfaces); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P1 rwb-source-data (Source data)/RWB P1 E1064 CON Data dictionary for the 14 data products - contract v1.md section 12.5 (the reference-table handler for table code sys_fields, called by the reference-data contract of rwb-case) and 12.2 (the list read of rwb-case); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/RWB P4 AD010 APP Approve a reference data load v1.md (the lov-loads approve gate calls the owner's approve)
section: RWB-P4-E1064-APP sections 1, 4 (steps 5 to 9), 5 (X9), 12.2, 12.5, 12.8 and 13: the call the gate makes after its checks pass, the table code it names, and the answer it returns to the approver
description: Three statements now describe the same apply step and none of them is the whole path. The legacy story submits the load through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads and applies it through DataDictionaryLoader.apply inside P1. In the target the load is submitted through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07), the rows land in P1's sys_fields through the reference-table handler that contract calls, and the module's own approve operation (API-P4-006) is P4's gate. No source says whether an approval passes through rwb-case's POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve, through P1's handler, or through both in that order. This story takes the reading that keeps one writer and one approver: rwb-case owns the load and moves the version, P1 applies the rows through its handler, and rwb-access decides the gate and writes nothing.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-064 section 4 steps 2 and 3 and section 12 (two endpoints and one Java interface, all on the monolith base /api/recovery/v1); P1 E1064 CON section 12.5 (the handler is what replaces DataDictionaryLoader, called by the rwb-case contract) and section 12.2 (the list read is P3's); TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006 (the submit and the approve on the module's surface, no apply step named); P4 AD010 APP (the gate calls the owner's approve for the lov-load family); Templates and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-07 and DP-11 (contract with mock, one hop)
proposed: Confirm the apply order with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-access: the load owner moves the version after the gate passes, the dictionary owner applies the rows through its reference-table handler, and the gate answers the decision and writes no row. Publish that order in the two contracts (RWB-P1-E1064-CON and the rwb-case reference-data contract) and in the reference-load handler note. At D1 number this row GAP-nnnn and cite it from ASM-B2-P4-020-4.
